description: A Yuan army advances into Mian and reaches Pagan; the Yuan dynastic account then records losses and a tributary settlement.
sourceCitation: Yuan shi 元史, juan 210, Mian 緬 entry, Zhiyuan 23-24 account (Chinese Text Project aligned text/translation)
geometryStatus: Pagan city/campaign-region marker; no reconstructed route or battle point
reviewReason: Yuan shi juan 210 records the advance reaching Pugan in Zhiyuan 24; official loss figures and the compressed claim that Mian was thereby pacified are not promoted

description: Nayan 乃顏 (Nǎiyán) rebels in 1287 and is defeated and captured; campaigns against allied and surviving rebel groups continue into 1288.
sourceCitation: Yuan shi 元史, juan 133, Tachu zhuan 塔出傳 and related campaign biographies (Chinese original; my translation for atlas wording)
secondCitation: Yuan shi jishi benmo 元史紀事本末, juan 2, Beibian zhuwang zhi luan 北邊諸王之亂, Zhiyuan 24-25 (Chinese original chronological reconciliation; my translation)
geometryStatus: eastern steppe-Liaodong campaign region; no exact battle point, pursuit line, camp polygon or reconstructed imperial route
reviewReason: Yuan dynastic biographies independently attest Nayan’s rebellion, imperial campaign, defeat and pursuit; Chinese chronological synthesis preserves the 1287 opening and continuation against remaining groups into 1288 without promoting discovery totals or an exact battlefield point

description: Third Mongol-Yuan invasion of Đại Việt and Bạch Đằng withdrawal disaster
sourceCitation: https://zh.wikisource.org/zh-hant/%E5%A4%A7%E8%B6%8A%E5%8F%B2%E8%A8%98%E5%85%A8%E6%9B%B8/%E6%9C%AC%E7%B4%80%E5%8D%B7%E4%B9%8B%E4%BA%94
geometryStatus: 1287-1288 Đại Việt campaign region plus Bạch Đằng river-section marker only; no inferred invasion route, exact stake field, fleet tracks, battle footprint, or retreat corridor
reviewReason: Dai Viet su ky toan thu book 5 records the 1287-1288 invasion, failed rendezvous with grain ships, withdrawal decision, and March 1288 Bach Dang fighting with planted stakes and captures; Yuan shi 209 independently records the invasion, missing grain fleet, withdrawal, and contested exit. Model a campaign parent with Bach Dang as terminal withdrawal phase, not a single battle-only event.

description: A Yuan expedition sails for Java in late 1292, lands and campaigns by water and land in 1293, then withdraws after its Javanese ally turns against it.
sourceCitation: Yuan shi 元史, juan 210, Jiawa 爪哇 entry (Chinese Text Project aligned text/translation)
geometryStatus: East Java coastal/river campaign region; no reconstructed fleet route or battlefield point
reviewReason: dynastic history gives dispatch, sailing, landing, combined advance, fighting and April withdrawal; official force/casualty numbers are not promoted

description: Kublai dies at Zitan Hall in 1294; Temür succeeds at Shangdu, closing the atlas module boundary.
sourceCitation: https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/%E5%85%83%E5%8F%B2/%E5%8D%B7017
geometryStatus: dated court-state markers at Zitan Hall and Shangdu only; no inferred funeral route, procession track, succession territory, frontier, or empire-control surface
reviewReason: Yuan shi juan 17 dates Kublai’s death at Zitan Hall in the first lunar month of Zhiyuan 31 and Temür’s accession at Shangdu in the fourth month. This is a material state-transition boundary for the declared c.1294 endpoint, not a battle or inferred territorial change.
